items.title: Meta signs 6-gigawatt AI chip deal with AMD

featured_image.name: AMD and Oracle announce agreement for 50,000 GPUs as AI deal ...

items.description:
Meta Platforms and AMD on Tuesday announced a multi-year, multi-generation agreement to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD Instinct GPUs for Meta's AI infrastructure, in a deal that could generate tens of billions of dollars in revenue for the chipmaker and reshape the competitive landscape of the AI hardware market.[1][2]

The partnership marks Meta's most direct move yet to diversify its AI compute supply chain beyond Nvidia, which secured its own sweeping deal with Meta just one week earlier. Under the agreement, AMD issued Meta a performance-based warrant for up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock — roughly 10% of the company — structured to vest as shipment milestones and stock price thresholds are achieved.[3][4][2]

items.title: Asian markets split as AI fears, new tariffs rattle investors

featured_image.name: EU pauses U.S. trade deal as it seeks clarity over Trump's new 15% global tariffs

items.description:
Asian stocks diverged on Tuesday as markets across the region absorbed a sharp Wall Street selloff driven by fresh concerns about artificial intelligence displacing legacy businesses, while a new 10% global tariff imposed by President Donald Trump took effect just days after the Supreme Court struck down his original trade duties.

Japan's Nikkei 225 surged 0.9% to 57,354 as markets reopened from a holiday, lifted by gains in semiconductor-related stocks. South Korea's Kospi climbed 1.8% to a record 5,951.90, powered by Samsung Electronics, which jumped 3.2%, and SK Hynix, up 4.8%. Mainland China also rallied on its return from Lunar New Year, with the Shanghai Composite rising 1.2%. But Hong Kong's Hang Seng fell 1.9% to 26,564 as traders locked in profits from a recent rally.[1][2][3]

items.title: MIT study rules out wildfires, volcanoes as cause of recent surface warming

featured_image.name: Climate 'fingerprints' mark human activity from the top of the ...

items.description:
A team of MIT scientists has isolated the distinct global temperature effects of three landmark natural events — the 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo, the 2019-2020 Australian wildfires, and the 2022 Hunga Tonga underwater volcanic eruption — using decades of satellite data and a novel signal-to-noise approach, according to a study published this week in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.[1][2]

The findings show that while all three events left measurable marks on atmospheric temperatures, none appear to explain the accelerating warming trend at Earth's surface in recent years, pointing instead to human activity as the dominant driver.[3][1]

items.title: Bitcoin drops below $63,000 as Trump's 15% tariff takes effect

featured_image.name: Trump tariffs live updates: Trump raises 'global' tariff to 15%; US to stop collecting duties deemed illegal

items.description:
Bitcoin tumbled more than 5% on Tuesday, sliding below $63,000 as a new round of global tariffs took effect and escalating tensions in the Middle East pushed investors further away from risk assets. The leading cryptocurrency fell to a low of $62,964.64, according to CNBC, as market participants engaged in what analysts described as broad "tactical de-risking."[1]

The drop coincided with the midnight implementation of President Donald Trump's 15% global import tariff under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 — a statute never before invoked by a president. Trump signed the measure on February 20, initially setting the rate at 10%, before raising it to the statutory maximum of 15% the following day via a post on Truth Social. The move came just hours after the U.S. Supreme Court, in a 6-3 ruling in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, struck down the administration's previous tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act.[2][3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: Oil prices near 7-month highs as U.S.-Iran talks loom

featured_image.name: Oil hovers below seven-month high as traders eye U.S.–Iran talks ...

items.description:
Oil prices hovered near seven-month highs on Tuesday as traders weighed the prospect of a new round of U.S.-Iran nuclear talks against an increasingly bellicose tone from President Donald Trump, who warned Tehran of a "very bad day" if negotiations fail.

Brent crude futures rose 0.8% to $72.08 a barrel in early Asian trade on Tuesday, nearing their highest level since late July, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude climbed 0.9% to $66.88 a barrel. Both benchmarks had touched their firmest levels in roughly seven months during Monday's session, with Brent reaching $72.50 and WTI hitting $67.28, before pulling back.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rival studies clash over fate of massive dying star WOH G64

featured_image.name: SALT solves stellar mystery: WOH G64 still alive as a red ...

items.description:
WOH G64, one of the most extreme stars ever observed, is at the center of a scientific debate over whether it is on a path toward imminent destruction or simply behaving strangely under the influence of a companion star.

A study published February 23 in Nature Astronomy by a team led by Gonzalo Muñoz-Sanchez concludes that WOH G64 has undergone a "dramatic transition" from a red supergiant to a yellow hypergiant, a rare and unstable phase that can precede a supernova explosion. The researchers analyzed more than three decades of photometric and spectroscopic data, finding that the star's effective temperature increased by more than 1,000 degrees Kelvin since roughly 2014. They describe WOH G64 as a "rare, massive symbiotic binary system" and propose that the transition could result from the partial ejection of its outer envelope or the winding down of a decades-long eruption.[1][2][3]
